record.title: Large configuration-free sets over algebraic number fields
record.statement:
Let $K$ be an algebraic number field with ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$, and let $r,s\in\mathcal O_K$ be distinct and nonzero. Let $P(n,m)$ denote the configuration defined earlier in the paper, and let $d$ be the associated ambient dimension.

**Configuration-free sets conjecture.** For every $C>0$, there exist $N\in\mathbb N$ and a set $B\subseteq\{0,1,\dots,N-1\}^d$ such that

$$
|B|>CN^{d/2}
$$

and $B$ contains no configuration $P(n,m)$ with $m\ne0$.

This would provide the quantitative configuration-free sets needed for the proposed counterexamples, extending the known motivation from the Gaussian-integer case and Behrend-type constructions.
record.source_name: Ethan Ackelsberg, Vitaly Bergelson and Andrew Best, “Multiple recurrence and large intersections for abelian group actions”, arXiv:2101.02811 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.02811

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2021).

record.title: The packing problem for square-free monomial ideals
record.statement:
Let $I$ be a square-free monomial ideal. Its **symbolic power** is $I^{(m)}=P_1^m\cap\cdots\cap P_s^m$ when $I=P_1\cap\cdots\cap P_s$ is its irredundant prime decomposition. The ideal $I$ has the **packing property** if every ideal obtained from $I$ by setting a subset of variables to $0$ and a disjoint subset to $1$ is König, meaning that it contains a set of pairwise coprime monomials of cardinality $\operatorname{ht}(I)$. **The packing problem.** The symbolic and ordinary powers coincide,

$$
I^{(m)}=I^m
$$

for every positive integer $m$, if and only if $I$ has the packing property. This conjecture connects symbolic-power equality with combinatorial packing properties of hypergraphs and remains unresolved in general.
record.source_name: Hrishikesh Bodas, Benjamin Drabkin, Caleb Fong, Su Jin, Justin Kim, Wenxuan Li, Alexandra Seceleanu, Tingting Tang and Brendan Williams, “Consequences of the packing problem”, arXiv:2101.04010 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.04010

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2021).

record.title: The regular-pattern conjecture for correctability in grid-like topologies
record.statement:
Let $m,n,a,b,h$ be non-negative integers with $m>a$ and $n>b$, and let 
$$
be an erasure pattern in the grid $[m]\times[n]$. In the topology $T_{m\times n}(a,b,0)$, call
$$
 **regular** if, for every $\subseteq[m]$ and $\subseteq[n]$ with $||=u\geq a$ and $||=v\geq b$, one has

$$
|\cap(\times)|\leq va+ub-ab.
$$

**Regular-pattern conjecture.** An erasure pattern $\mathcal{E}$ is correctable for the topology $T_{m\times n}(a,b,0)$ if and only if it is regular.

It is known that every non-regular pattern is not correctable, while the converse is established only for some parameter choices; the general equivalence remains open.

record.title: Derangement reciprocal-product congruences
record.statement:
For a positive integer $n$, let $D(n)=\{\tau\in S_n:\tau(j)\ne j\text{ for all }j=1,\ldots,n\}$ be the set of derangements, and let $\operatorname{sign}(\tau)$ denote the sign of a permutation. **Derangement congruences.** For any odd prime $p$,

$$
\sum_{\tau\in D(p-1)}\prod_{j=1}^{p-1}\frac{1}{j-\tau(j)}\equiv\left(\frac{-1}{p}\right)\pmod{p^2}
$$

and

$$
\sum_{\tau\in D(p-1)}\operatorname{sign}(\tau)\prod_{j=1}^{p-1}\frac{1}{j-\tau(j)}\equiv1\pmod{p^2}.
$$

These congruences concern derangement-restricted permanent- and determinant-type sums; the supplied text gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Zhi-Wei Sun, “On some determinants and permanents”, arXiv:2207.13039 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.13039

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2022).

record.title: Conjecture that planar grazes characterize ellipsoids
record.statement: Let $K,L\subset\mathbb R^n$ be convex bodies with $L\subset\operatorname{int}K$. For a point $x\in\mathbb R^n\setminus L$, let $\Sigma(L,x)$ denote the graze of $L$ from $x$, namely the intersection of the boundary of the support cone of $L$ from $x$ with $\partial L$. Suppose that, for every $x\in\partial K$, $\Sigma(L,x)$ lies in a hyperplane. **Planar-graze characterization conjecture.** Then $L$ is an ellipsoid. The source presents this as an expected extension of known characterizations of ellipsoids by planar shadow boundaries and grazes; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Ivan Gonzalez Garcia, Jesus Jeronimo Castro, Diana Janett Verdusco Hernandez and Efren Morales Amaya, “A characterization of the ellipsoid through planar grazes”, arXiv:2207.13294 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.13294

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2022). “This conjecture was first proved by P. W. Aitchison, C. M. Petty, and C. A. Rogers and is known as the False Centre Theorem.”

record.title: Uniform anti-concentration conjecture for the independence number of sparse random graphs
record.statement:
Let $G_{n,p}$ be the binomial random graph with $n$ vertices, where $p=n^{\gamma}$ and $-1<\gamma<-2/3$, and let $\alpha(G_{n,p})$ denote its independence number. For an arbitrary sequence $k=k(n)$, **Uniform anti-concentration conjecture.**

$$
\mathbb{P}\left(\alpha(G_{n,p})=k\right)=\widetilde{O}\left(n^{1+3\gamma/2}\right).
$$

This is proposed as a strengthening of the cited theorem and would give a uniform upper bound on every point probability in the regime $-1<\gamma<-2/3$; the supplied text gives no evidence that it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Tom Bohman and Jakob Hofstad, “Two-Point Concentration of the Independence Number of the Random Graph”, arXiv:2208.00117 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.00117

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2022).

record.title: The prime graph odd-prime labeling conjecture
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph. A graph is **prime** if it admits a prime labeling, and **odd prime** if its vertices can be injectively labeled by $1,3,\ldots,2|V(G)|-1$ so that adjacent vertices receive relatively prime labels. **Prime graph odd-prime conjecture.** Every prime graph is odd prime. No graph known to the authors is prime without being odd prime, while many graphs are known to be odd prime without being prime; the conjecture was previously introduced in the cited literature and remains open.
record.source_name: Holly Carter and N. Bradley Fox, “Odd Prime Graph Labelings”, arXiv:2208.08488 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.08488

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2022).

record.title: Nathan Williams's periodicity conjecture for trapezoids
record.statement:
Let $p$ be an integer with $p>1$, let $s\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $P$ be the subposet

$$
\{(i,k)\in[p]\times[p]\mid i+k>p+1\text{ and }i\leq k\text{ and }k\geq s\}
$$

of $[p]\times[p]$. Let $f\in\mathbb{K}^{\widehat{P}}$ be a $\mathbb{K}$-labeling such that $R^pf\neq\operatorname{\bot}$, and set $a=f(0)$ and $b=f(1)$. **Nathan Williams's trapezoid periodicity conjecture.** The elements $a$ and $b$ are invertible, and for every $x\in\widehat{P}$,

$$
(R^pf)(x)=a\overline{b}\cdot f(x)\cdot\overline{a}b.
$$

This is presented as a noncommutative extension of Nathan Williams's conjecture in the commutative setting; the supplied text does not state a resolution.
record.source_name: Darij Grinberg and Tom Roby, “Birational rowmotion on a rectangle over a noncommutative ring”, arXiv:2208.11156 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.11156

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2022).

record.title: Frankl's even-parity conjecture for t-intersecting k-Sperner families
record.statement:
Let $n$ and $t$ be integers with $n+t$ even and $n>t$, and let ${\mathcal F}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ be a **$t$-intersecting** family, meaning that $|F\cap F'|\geq t$ for all $F,F'\in{\mathcal F}$, and a **$k$-Sperner** family, meaning that it contains no chain of $k+1$ distinct sets under inclusion. **Frankl's conjecture.** One has

$$
|{\mathcal F}|\leq\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\binom{n}{\frac{n+t}{2}+i}.
$$

The bound is tight if true, attained by $\bigcup_{i=0}^{k-1}\binom{[n]}{\frac{n+t}{2}+i}$.
record.source_name: József Balogh, William B. Linz and Balázs Patkós, “On the sizes of t-intersecting k-chain-free families”, arXiv:2209.01656 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.01656

record.title: The Alternate Thomassé conjecture on sibling numbers of relations
record.statement:
Let $R=(V,E)$ be a relation of arbitrary cardinality, where $V$ is a non-empty domain and $E$ is an $n$-ary relation on $V$ for some positive integer $n$. The **sibling number** $Sib(R)$ is the number of isomorphism classes of relations equimorphic to $R$, where two relations are equimorphic when each embeds in the other.

**The Alternate Thomassé conjecture.** For every relation $R$ of arbitrary cardinality,

$$
Sib(R)=1\quad\text{or}\quad\infty.
$$

This is the unrestricted-cardinality alternative to Thomassé's conjecture and is the version addressed for countable $NE$-free posets in the paper. The supplied text gives no evidence that the conjecture has been resolved in general.
record.source_name: Davoud Abdi, “A Proof of the Alternate Thomassé Conjecture for Countable NE-Free Posets”, arXiv:2209.03893 (2023).

record.title: Akbari–Dalirrooyfard–Ehsani–Ozeki–Sherkati list-avoiding orientation conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and let $F:V(G)\to 2^{\mathbb{N}}$. An orientation $D$ of $G$ is **$F$-avoiding** if $\deg_D^+(v)\notin F(v)$ for every $v\in V(G)$. **The list-avoiding orientation conjecture.** If

$$
|F(v)|\leq \frac{1}{2}(\deg_G(v)-1)
$$

for each $v\in V(G)$, then $G$ has an $F$-avoiding orientation. This strengthens the earlier bound with $\frac14$ and is sharp if true; related results are known for spanning subgraphs, but the orientation statement remains open.
record.source_name: Peter Bradshaw, Yaobin Chen, Hao Ma, Bojan Mohar and Hehui Wu, “List-avoiding orientations”, arXiv:2209.09107 (2024).

record.title: Monotonicity conjecture for the number of rainbow trees
record.statement:
Let $k,c,c'\in\mathbb{N}$ with $c'\leq c$, and let $G$ be a graph. For $r\in\{c,c'\}$, let $T(r,k)$ be the random variable counting the number of rainbow trees of order $k$ when the edges of $G$ are coloured uniformly with $r$ colours. **Rainbow-tree monotonicity conjecture.** The random variable $T(c,k)$ stochastically dominates $T(c',k)$.

A coupling establishing this monotonicity is immediate when $c=2c'$, but a general coupling was not found. The conjecture formalises the intuition that using more colours should make rainbow substructures more abundant.
record.source_name: Oliver Cooley, Tuan Anh Do, Joshua Erde and Michael Missethan, “The emergence of a giant rainbow component”, arXiv:2210.11972 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.11972

record.title: Conjecture on monochromatic Gower sum and product subspaces
record.statement: Let $X_k$ be the underlying set of the Gower subspaces, and let $X_k=\bigcup_{i=1}^r C_i$ be a finite partition. A Gower sum subspace is generated by a subset $A=\{\mathbf{n_i}:i\in I\}\subset X_k$, while a product subspace is generated by a subset $B=\{\mathbf{m_i}:i\in I\}\subset X_k$. **Monochromatic Gower subspace conjecture.** For every $k,r\in\mathbb{N}$ and every such partition, there exist subsets $A$ and $B$ such that the Gower sum subspace generated by $A$ and the product subspace generated by $B$ are both contained in the same color class $C_i$. This would unify the additive and multiplicative Ramsey phenomena established separately in the paper, but the combined monochromatic conclusion is presented as a conjecture and its resolution is not supplied here.
record.source_name: Sayan Goswami, “Additive and multiplicative Gower's Ramsey theorem”, arXiv:2210.16073 (2022).

record.title: Golomb–Moreno conjecture on circular Costas sequences
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{Z}_n$ denote the cyclic group of order $n$. A **circular Costas sequence** is equivalent to an injective map $\varphi:\mathbb{Z}_n\to\mathbb{Z}_{n+1}$ whose difference maps

$$
\Delta_{\varphi,k}:\mathbb{Z}_n\to\mathbb{Z}_{n+1},\qquad i\mapsto\varphi(i+k)-\varphi(i)
$$

are injective for every nonzero $k\in\mathbb{Z}_n$. A Welch sequence is obtained from the Welch construction over a finite field. **Golomb–Moreno's conjecture.** A Costas sequence is circular if and only if it is Welch. Circular Costas sequences form a stronger class than singly periodic sequences, and the conjecture asserts that the Welch construction gives all of them; its resolution is not established in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Ivelisse Rubio and Jaziel Torres, “Circular Costas maps: a multidimensional analog of circular Costas sequences”, arXiv:2210.16661 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.16661

record.title: Chromatic symmetric homology interval conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $span_0(G)$ denote the homological span of its degree-$0$ chromatic symmetric homology.

**Chromatic symmetric homology interval conjecture.** The groups $H_{i,0}(G;\mathbb{C})$ are non-trivial for every integer $i$ satisfying

$$
0 \leq i \leq span_0(G)-1.
$$

This conjecture concerns the absence of gaps in the nonzero homological degrees of degree-$0$ chromatic symmetric homology. The source presents it as an open question left by earlier work; its status is otherwise unresolved here.
record.source_name: Azzurra Ciliberti, “A deletion-contraction long exact sequence for chromatic symmetric homology”, arXiv:2211.00699 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.00699

record.title: Equivalence of partition regularity over polynomial and integer patterns
record.statement: Let $T$ denote the polynomial setting used in the paper, and let $\mathbb{N}$ denote the positive integers. A polynomial pattern $\mathcal{F}$ is **partition regular** over a domain if every finite coloring of that domain contains a monochromatic realization of $\mathcal{F}$. **Polynomial–integer equivalence conjecture.** A polynomial pattern $\mathcal{F}$ is partition regular over $T$ if and only if it is partition regular over $\mathbb{N}$. The paper has already shown that partition regularity over $T$ implies partition regularity over $\mathbb{N}$ with primitive recursive bounds, while the converse is posed as an open conjectural strengthening.
record.source_name: Ryan Alweiss, “Monochromatic Sums and Products of Polynomials”, arXiv:2211.00766 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.00766

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2022).

record.title: Monomial positivity conjecture for H-graph ideals
record.statement: Let $P$ be a $(\mathbf{3}+\mathbf{1})$-free poset, let $I_H^P$ be the corresponding $H$-graph ideal, and let $\mathfrak{m}^P_\lambda(\mathbf{u})$ be the elements defined in the source. Say that an element is **$\mathbf{u}$-monomial positive modulo $I_H^P$** if it has a representative that is a positive sum of monomials in the noncommuting variables $\mathbf{u}$. **Monomial positivity conjecture.** For every such $P$ and partition $\lambda$, $\mathfrak{m}^P_\lambda(\mathbf{u})$ is $\mathbf{u}$-monomial positive modulo $I_H^P$; consequently, for every $I_H^P$-graph $\Gamma$, $\omega F_\Gamma(\mathbf{x})$ is $e$-positive. The supplied text gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Jonah Blasiak, Holden Eriksson, Pavlo Pylyavskyy and Isaiah Siegl, “Noncommutative Schur functions for posets”, arXiv:2211.03967 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.03967

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2022). “This conjecture was proven several years later by Brosnan and Chow and independently by Guay-Paquet .”

record.title: Nebbia's CCR conjecture for boundary-transitive groups on semi-regular trees
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a thick semi-regular tree, and let $G$ be a closed subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}(T)$ acting transitively on the boundary $\partial T$. A locally compact group $G$ is **CCR** if $\pi(f)$ is compact for every irreducible representation $\pi$ of $G$ and every $f\in L^1(G)$. **Nebbia's conjecture.** Every such group $G$ is CCR.

The conjecture proposes that sufficiently regular boundary action forces regularity of the unitary dual. Earlier results establish implications from CCR or Type I assumptions to boundary transitivity, while the converse remains open in this generality.
record.source_name: Lancelot Semal, “Irreducibly represented Lie groups and Nebbia's CCR conjecture on trees”, arXiv:2306.04310 (2023).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2022–2023). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2203.04189](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.04189).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.04310

record.title: The strong Fox conjecture for alternating knots
record.statement:
Let $K \subset S^3$ be an alternating knot. Its Alexander polynomial is

$$
\Delta_K(t)=\sum a_i t^i.
$$

Here a polynomial is **log-concave** when its coefficient sequence satisfies $a_{i-1}a_{i+1}\leq a_i^2$ for every relevant index. **Strong Fox conjecture.** The Alexander polynomial $\Delta_K(t)$ is log-concave. This strengthens Fox's trapezoidal conjecture, since log-concave sequences are unimodal. The conjecture concerns a broad class of alternating knots and is motivated by the extensive evidence for unimodality of their Alexander-polynomial coefficients.
record.source_name: Ian M. Banfield, “Christoffel words and the strong Fox conjecture for two-bridge knots”, arXiv:2212.04561 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.04561

record.title: The Sperner-system strengthening of Snevily's conjecture
record.statement:
Let $n,s$ be integers with $n\geq 2s-1$, let $L=\{\ell_{1},\ell_{2},\ldots,\ell_{s}\}$ be a set of $s$ non-negative integers, and let an **$L$-intersecting Sperner system** be a Sperner family $\mathcal{F}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ such that $|F\cap F'|\in L$ for every distinct $F,F'\in\mathcal{F}$. **The Sperner-system strengthening.** Every such family satisfies

$$
|\mathcal{F}|\leq\binom{n}{s}.
$$

The source presents this as a stronger conjecture than Snevily's conjecture. The bound is immediate from the LYM inequality when $n<2s-1$, while the stated range is not settled in the supplied text.
